Mean (average) is sensitive to outliers; median (middle value, sorted) is resistant. Range = max − min. IQR = Q3 − Q1 (middle 50 % of data; also resistant to outliers). Standard deviation: the SAT never asks you to compute it — it asks you to compare or interpret it. A larger SD means greater spread around the mean.

body.en: A random sample allows generalisation to the population it was drawn from — no further. Voluntary-response and convenience samples are biased. Observational studies can show association only; establishing causation requires a randomised controlled experiment (random assignment to groups). A margin of error creates a confidence interval: estimate ± margin of error.

A poll of 600 voters finds 54 % support Candidate A, margin of error ±3 %.

True support is estimated to be between 51 % and 57 %. Since the entire interval exceeds 50 %, the data support a majority — but only for the population sampled.

label.en: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Rates, Percentages & Data Analysis

body.en:
• Percent Change Base Denominator: \( \text{Percent Change} = \frac{\text{New} - \text{Old}}{\text{Old}} \times 100\% \). The denominator is always the original starting value. If an item drops from \( 80 to \)60, the percent decrease is \( \frac{20}{80} = 25\% \), NOT \( \frac{20}{60} = 33.3\% \).
  • Square and Cubic Unit Conversions: Linear conversions must be raised to the appropriate power. \( 1\text{ yard} = 3\text{ feet} \implies 1\text{ sq yard} = 3^2 = 9\text{ sq feet} \).
  • Residual Sign: \( \text{Residual} = \text{Actual } y - \text{Predicted } \hat{y} \). Points above the line of best fit have positive residuals; points below have negative residuals.
  • Causation vs. Association: Only randomized experiments can establish cause-and-effect. Observational surveys can only demonstrate correlation/association.

question.en: A retailer reduces the price of a winter jacket by 25%. Two weeks later, the retailer reduces the sale price by an additional 20%. The final price is $96. What was the original price of the jacket before any discounts?

solution.en:
Let \( P \) be the original price. After the first 25% discount, the price is \( P(1 - 0.25) = 0.75P \). After the additional 20% discount on the sale price, the multiplier is \( (1 - 0.20) = 0.80 \):

\[ (0.80)(0.75)P = 96 \implies 0.60P = 96 \implies P = \frac{96}{0.60} = 160. \]

The original price was $160.

question.en:
SAT-style: A researcher randomly assigns 50 students to a tutoring programme and 50 to a control group, then compares test scores. Which conclusion is best supported if the tutored group scores significantly higher?

(A) Tutoring causes higher scores.
(B) There is an association but causation cannot be determined.
(C) Results apply to all students nationwide.
(D) The sample size is too small to draw any conclusion.

solution.en: (A). Random assignment to groups (not just observation) allows a causal conclusion. Results generalise to the population sampled, not all students, so (C) is wrong.
